findings.finding: F1: the 32-row half of INFRA-63's tail rule would keep deleted text for ever (LEGION-496, CHANGELOG.md:1920) and leave a 28-version document never compacted; history_memory_test's stored-bytes bound would fail.
findings.answer: Raised with INFRA-63's architect, who dropped the 32-row half (2026-10-27T04:49Z): compaction folds only rows older than 2 minutes, on every path. LEGION-496's guarantee now holds within about 75 minutes (D3, departure 3). The memory tests backdate created_at before the deploy-style stop.

findings.finding: F2: 'flat cost' across 1/30/240 versions is not machine-checkable and the planner's data says the state itself grows 150 KB to 1.18 MB.
findings.answer: Departure 1: acceptance 6 replaces it with BenchmarkRoomLoad pass conditions (one row vs one row plus 15 young rows within 1.25x; 240/120 and 120/60 each at most 2.3x; 240-version load at least 3x cheaper than main), benchstat over -count 10, documents backdated and compacted.

findings.finding: F3: the upload's 60% production cost is the room's own decode (loadRoom -> ApplyUpdateV1), which compaction does not move.
findings.answer: Measured: 70% of decoding a 240-writer state is ygo resolveWithinUpdatePending; increasing client ids remove it (391 -> 120 ms). D6 fixes the decoder in the ygo fork (departure 2). Acceptance 7's profile splits upload CPU into fold, validateUpdate, ygo room decode and the rest.

findings.finding: F4: merging rows for loads (MergeUpdatesV1) keeps deleted content (LEGION-496's 1,842 MiB failure), drops the read-back check, and dropping validateUpdate loses failRoom.
findings.answer: D4 keeps the streaming fold and its read-back for loads; rows are buffered only up to 32 MiB, else streamed in the transaction as today. validateUpdate is skipped only when Load already read back the state, and kept for a single stored row, so failRoom still runs.

findings.finding: F5: lock-free fold needs: cursor read in the write transaction, recoverPruneTx, (version, xmin) of every folded row, re-queue stop condition and backoff, negative cache for unfoldable logs, fold into the newest foldable row, stamp/preload comments and the stamp test.
findings.answer: D1 step 3 and acceptance 4 cover each case (prune, stranded checkpoint, rebuild, delete, concurrent and older-build compaction, cursor advance, misread). Backoff 1 s to 1 min; negative cache keyed by the fold point's (version, xmin). D7 and the tests list fix the comments and read_cache_test:139-160.

findings.finding: F6: appends during a burst are all younger than 2 minutes; benchmarks need backdating; shutdown and the failed-room path; dead CompactEvery.
findings.answer: D2's queue re-checks a room when its oldest unfolded row turns 2 (or 15) minutes old. Tests and benchmarks backdate created_at in SQL. Shutdown stops the worker before pools close; room-close compaction stays inline on ygo's worker with the tail rule; one implementation, failed rooms only wait for the lock. CompactEvery=200 removed.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance: a benchmark loads documents with 1, 30 and 240 versions and shows flat cost.
specDepartures.plan: Acceptance 6: the cost no longer depends on the number of stored updates (one row vs one row plus 15 young rows within 1.25x) and grows at most linearly with writers (240/120 and 120/60 each at most 2.3x), with the 240-version load at least 3x cheaper than main and before/after numbers stated.
specDepartures.evidence: Planner's probe (dispatch://INFRA-593/artifact/infra-593-load-probe-go-txt): the compacted state grows 150 KB to 1.18 MB over 240 versions (116,639 deleted clock units beside 108,629 live, as Yjs keeps them); a fresh 1.18 MB document decodes in 26 ms against 3.9 ms for 150 KB. Only discarding history would make it flat, which closes open editors and loses offline browser edits.

acceptance: The cost of loading a room no longer grows with the document's version count: a benchmark loads documents with 1, 30 and 240 versions (the LINUX specs written on 2026-10-26 had a median of 28 and a maximum of 237) and shows flat cost.
